title: fix(app-shell): the lifecycle badge draws for an authoring caller only
body:
Fixes #12194

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`ManagedByBadge` reads `useCanAuthorMetadata()` and renders nothing for a caller who cannot author metadata. Triage ruled the badge an authoring aid (option a, comment 6120170778). The check lives inside the badge, so the three pages that draw it follow one rule: the record page, the object list header and the record form page. No new prop, export, spec key or i18n key. `ManagedByBadge` is not exported from `@object-ui/app-shell`, and its signature is unchanged. Comments at the three call sites say where the check lives.

Effect: an end user opening a `better-auth` record sees no "Identity" badge (zh-CN shows 「身份」), for example on the cloud workspace page (`sys_organization`). An authoring caller still sees it.

## Measured before coding (the dispatch's three mechanism assumptions)

1. **The capability and its fail-open branch.** `useCanAuthorMetadata()` returns `hasCapabilities(['manage_metadata'])`. `MePermissionsProvider.hasCapabilities` returns `true` only when `systemPermissions` is not an array. The framework's `GET /api/v1/auth/me/permissions` (objectstack `plugin-hono-server`, `current-user-endpoints.ts`, read at objectstack `6a40a09ed`) always sends `systemPermissions: Array.from(...)` on its success path.
   - **An end user on a deployment that serves the endpoint does NOT see the badge.**
   - The check fails open (badge shown, as before) in three cases: the endpoint's branch when the security plugin is not wired, which sends no `systemPermissions` (the server itself fails open there); the endpoint's catch branch; and a host that mounts no permission provider.
   - The fail-open rule is unchanged, and a test pins it.
2. **Per-object authoring check.** app-shell has none. Every authoring entry point reads the global `useCanAuthorMetadata`: HomePage's builder CTAs, AppHeader's Studio bridge, PageView's edit pencil and the metadata-admin read-only gates. AppHeader and PageView also require `isAdmin` for their editor entry points. The badge uses the capability alone, as the ruling names it. No new capability.
3. **The three sites and what each is for.** All three are authoring aids, so the rule applies to each:
   - **Record page** (`RecordDetailView`, the card's site): drawn in the view's own chrome above the page tree. Edit affordances are already gated by the bucket.
   - **List header** (`ObjectView`): every caller still has the toolbar's hidden New/Import/Delete and the read-only buckets' empty state (`resolveManagedByEmptyState`). Neither reads the badge.
   - **Form page** (`RecordFormPage`): the dispatch asked whether the badge explains read-only fields to an end user. It does not. That sentence is plugin-form's `ClosedAffordanceNotice` (objectui#11000), drawn from `closedFormAffordance`, the same verdict that locks the fields. I also corrected the badge-site comment, which said forms disable inputs for every non-`platform` bucket. That is not true: `config` and `system-data` are writable.

## Tests

The three new files mount the real view under the real `MePermissionsProvider` (`initialPermissions`), so the chain under test is the shipped one: badge, then `useCanAuthorMetadata`, then `usePermissions`, then the provider's `hasCapabilities`. An absence is read only after the page has painted, and the authoring case renders the badge in the same harness.

- `RecordDetailView.managedByBadgeAuthoring-12194.test.tsx`: end user sees none; author sees `better-auth`; CONTROL: no `managedBy` draws none for author or end user; CONTROL: `platform` draws none for the author; an answer with no `systemPermissions` draws the badge (the fail-open rule, unchanged).
- `ObjectView.managedByBadgeAuthoring-12194.test.tsx` and `RecordFormPage.managedByBadgeAuthoring-12194.test.tsx`: end user sees none, author sees it, and the no-`managedBy` CONTROL for both callers.

**Ablation (one-off, no file kept).** With the `if (!canAuthor) return null;` line replaced by a marker through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor count 1 to 0, marker 0 to 1, blob `8d5e4835a52d` to `1ce4cbfec118`. The tests import the views and the badge relatively from `src`, so nothing was built. Prediction, written in each file's header before the run: the three end-user cases go RED and everything else stays GREEN. Observed: `Tests  3 failed | 8 passed (11)`, and the three failures were exactly those cases. Restore was proven: blob equals HEAD (`8d5e4835a52d`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Gates (worktree HEAD `4c026221`, unless a line names another sha)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: exit 0. It ran after building the upstream closure with `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` (exit 0). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists all three new test files and `ManagedByBadge.tsx`. A first attempt without the closure built exited 2 on `TS2307` for workspace imports. That is a missing prerequisite, not a measurement.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell lint` (`eslint .`): exit 0.
- Tests, narrowed (declared): the three new files, 11/11 at `4c026221`. Plus every app-shell and console test file that imports a view that draws the badge, or the shell that mounts them (`ObjectView`, `RecordDetailView`, `RecordFormPage`, `ObjectDataPage`, `InterfaceListPage`, `AppContent`, or `@object-ui/app-shell`), derived with `git grep` over test files: 166 files, all passed. 135 files / 1,135 tests ran at `28ef0f23`; 31 files / 312 tests ran at `4c026221`. The only change between those two commits is a typing cleanup in one new test file. The full app-shell suite is left to CI.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes` OK · `pnpm check:new-line-citations` `0 new citation(s)` · `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` OK · changeset presence / fixed / overwrite / claims OK · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` / `-inherit` / `-override-shape` OK · `check:test-path-roots` OK · `check:pending-changeset-literals` OK · type-check and lint coverage OK · `check:unreferenced-sources` OK · `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` with the 8 paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:eager-closure`, reason: it needs `apps/console/dist` (exit 2, `No eager-closure report`). The new import (`hooks/useCanAuthorMetadata`) is already imported by `AppHeader` and `HomePage`, so I expect no new module in the eager closure. Left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **Trade-off, intended by the ruling.** A non-authoring admin, such as an EE workspace owner (`organization_admin` withholds `manage_metadata`), no longer sees the `better-auth` tooltip's line about managing these records through the auth provider's flows. The `better-auth` list empty states still give that guidance to every caller.
- `utils/managedByEmptyState.ts` mirrors the badge's mapping for empty states. It is out of scope and untouched.
- Changeset: `.changeset/12194-managed-by-badge-authoring.md`, `@object-ui/app-shell` `patch`.
